text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Stiffer penalties await offending motorists if new proposed legislation is adopted. Speeding drivers in public service vehicles would face a minimum of six months in jail if caught, while rural bus operators would be required to compensate for the death or disability of passengers.

- Zimbabwean pressure groups have proposed a land tax on under-utilised land and have implored the government to limit to one each the number of farms owned by now-indigenous (non-black) farmers while allowing black farmers more.
- Only 42,000 tonnes of maize out of over 368,000 tonnes allocated to communal farmers under the grain loan scheme last year have so far been recovered by the government.
